kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1100.summary: Opens the divisio textus of Lombard's d.37 ('Et quoniam demonstratum est'): having treated the existence of things in God, the Master now treats God's existence in things, and the section divides in two.
claims: Distinction 37 shifts from things' existence in God to God's existence in things.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1112.summary: First main part: Lombard assigns the modes by which God is in things.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1117.summary: Second main part ('Cumque divina natura'): Lombard assigns the modes by which God is not in things.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1124.summary: The first main part divides into three.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1126.summary: First subpart: God's common mode of existing in things.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1131.summary: Second subpart ('In sanctis vero'): God's special mode of existing in the saints by grace.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1138.summary: Third subpart ('Ex praedictis patet'): God's mode of existing by nature.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1144.summary: The middle subpart, on indwelling in the saints, divides into four.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1146.summary: First, Lombard shows how God dwells in the saints.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1151.summary: Second ('Si autem quaeris'), he asks where God dwelt before there were saints.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1156.summary: Third ('Sciendum est etiam'), he shows that the whole Trinity dwells in the saints.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1163.summary: Fourth, he shows that God dwells not only in adult saints but also in regenerated infants, which is also remarkable.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1170.summary: The part beginning 'Ex praedictis', on God's existence in things by nature, divides into three.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1178.summary: First, the mode by which God is in all things by his incomprehensible nature.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1183.summary: Second ('Quidam tamen'), Lombard rebukes some people's presumption on this point.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1190.summary: Third ('Solet etiam'), he raises and solves an incidental doubt; then begins the second main part ('Cumque divina natura'), removing modes in which God is not in things, divided in two.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1201.summary: First, Lombard shows that God is not in things mutably, neither by local nor by temporal change.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1206.summary: Second ('Fateamur itaque'), he repeats and confirms this truth.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1217.summary: The first of these divides into three.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1220.summary: First, God is not in things mutably.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1225.summary: Second ('De mutatione loci'), Lombard raises and settles an incidental doubt about the change of created spirits.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1232.summary: Third ('Sunt ergo spiritus creati'), he concludes that only the uncreated spirit is simply immutable; then the part 'Fateamur itaque' divides in two.
claims: Only the uncreated spirit is simply immutable.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1241.summary: In the first part Lombard repeats and confirms what preceded.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1246.summary: In the second ('Ad hoc autem solet opponi') he raises and solves an objection.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1251.summary: Announces that three questions (articles) are raised about this distinction.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1257.summary: First article: God's existence in things.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1262.summary: Second article: the existence of an angel in place.

kzz7yh-a77141-d1e1267.summary: Third article: the motion of an angel from place to place.

kzz7yh-a77141.summary: The Praeambulum to I d.37 gives Richard's divisio textus of Lombard's distinction on God's existence in things and announces the article plan. Lombard first gives the modes by which God is in things: the common mode, the special indwelling of the whole Trinity in saints and regenerated infants, and presence by incomprehensible nature, with a rebuke of presumption. He then removes the modes in which God is not in things, chiefly mutability by local or temporal change, with an incidental discussion of the change of created spirits and the conclusion that only the uncreated spirit is simply immutable. Richard's questions follow: God's existence in things, the angel in place, and angelic local motion.
claims: Lombard's d.37 treats God's existence in things and excludes mutable modes of presence.
Richard's commentary on d.37 addresses God's presence, angelic location and angelic motion.
